text:
Samira N.: flagging an oddity from a private installation (eu-central, onprem edge). Decrypts are succeeding at the keystore-proxy but we have no corresponding audit envelope in the central store. can someone help triage?
Ben Ortiz: are the proxy -> KMS calls going via our audit sidecar? or is the proxy doing direct egress?
Samira N.: the proxy uses the sidecar in the chart. local proxy log shows `INFO decrypt ok id=kp-41a host=edge-7`. sidecar logs show POST 200 to gateway, but the audit pipeline never shows an envelope.
Priya S.: could the forwarder be dropping envelopes for priv installs? we have a policy change earlier this month around PII suppression (MR #812).
Tomas V.: MR #812 set payload redaction but shouldn't drop the envelope entirely. I'll check the forwarder code path that assembles the envelope; maybe an early return on empty payload.
audit-bot: audit-query kp-41a -> forwarded from edge-7 -> forwarder acked -> no envelope_create event detected.
Ben Ortiz: also check whether any iptables or host route on customer appliance bypasses the sidecar and reaches KMS directly. I've seen customer NAT rules that short-circuit the pod network.
Samira N.: i pulled the host's iptables: there's a MASQUERADE rule in nat POSTROUTING and a custom PREROUTING DNAT to 169.254.1.1:8443. that looks suspect.
Priya S.: we should make the proxy fail hard if it cannot reach the local auditor on startup. add a boot-time check for `localhost:4321/handshake` that must succeed else proxy enters degraded state and logs an explicit error.
Tomas V.: i can add the handshake + monotonic attestation entry. plan: during boot, proxy performs `POST /handshake {instance_id, version}` signed with instance key, forwarder records attestation with increasing counter. store counter in sealed local file.
Ben Ortiz: alternative idea: include an audit witness token we sign pre-call and append the KMS response digest post-call. proof chain lives in tenant audit store. note: some KMS gateways strip custom headers, so include the signed witness in the audit-store write before and after.
oncall-sre: for incident playbook, recommended steps: 1) capture /var/log/keystore-proxy.log 2) dump forwarder spool (db) 3) export iptables and `ip route` 4) get container env (NET_ADMIN bits) 5) escalate to sec. adding this to Runbook Keystore-Audit.
Priya S.: network policy suggestion to enforce sidecar path (k8s example):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: force-keystore-via-auditor
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-proxy
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: audit-forwarder
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 4321
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
      except: []
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
```
Samira N.: we should also publish a small iptables test that CI can run in a namespace: create a fake NAT rule to force direct egress and assert the forwarder receives nothing -> fail the test.
Tomas V.: i'll open MR #859 to add: 1) forwarder ensures envelope stub always created even when payload redacted 2) proxy startup handshake 3) runbook checklist update. assigning to @TomasV.
Ben Ortiz: small Q — what about SLA evidence for customers? adding witness tokens to the tenant audit store gives an unforgeable chain they can query. include a TTLed signature to avoid long-lived keys.
Priya S.: noted. I'll draft a short spec for witness lifecycle and key rotation. link draft: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/keystore-witness-spec (WIP).
Samira N.: thanks. let's sync for 15m tomorrow 09:30 CET to align on MR scope and runbook wording. :calendar:
